newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore stocks seen weak, electronics supported.
newsitem.headline: Singapore stocks seen weak, electronics supported.

text.p: Singapore shares were likely to remain weak, with investors eyeing regional currency developments and sidelined ahead of Singapore's June non-oil export figures due for release next week, dealers said.
"While Asian currencies appear to have quietened, investors still prefer a wait-and-see stance. They are also waiting for Singapore's export figures next week," said a dealer.
Dealers said there could be a slight correction to recent losses but expected any rebound to be short-lived.
"Sentiment is weak. We have to wait for the next set of financial results to get a clearer idea of performance," said another dealer with a Singapore house.

"Investors should be prepared that the Straits Times Industrials (STI) index would not return above 2,200 in the next three month without any major movements in index-linked stocks like Cerebos," he said.

Earlier in January, when the STI index was trading above 2,200, food company Cerebos shares were above S$10.00. The share price has since fallen to around S$6.00, dragging along with it the price-weighted STI index.
Dealers also expected a further rally in selective electronic shares following extremely strong gains in high-tech stocks on Nasdaq on Wednesday.
On Wednesday, the STI index ended 19.20 points down at 1,917.89. Support was seen at 1,900. Wall Street ended 63.17 up at 8,038.88.
